clue.text: Instances where arrested bounder goes down

indicators.note: something arrested is held in custody, so one word is held inside the other

parts.note: instances are cases, examples of something
a bounder is a cad, an ill-mannered man

explanation.surface: Episodes in which a rogue is taken into custody and sent down to prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes down' suggests a prison sentence, but it is the definition: water that cascades falls down. 'Where arrested' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To cascade is to fall in stages, as a waterfall pours downward.

clue.text: Fresh appeal to bring America into line gets loud support

indicators.note: one piece is put into the line of letters formed by the other
a fresh version is a new one, so the letters are made over in a new order

parts.note: US is short for United States, America

explanation.surface: A renewed plea to make the United States conform wins vocal backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' rearranges the first word to give APPLAE; 'into line' is the insertion signal, with 'to bring' only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Applause is clapping and cheering, a noisy show of approval.

clue.text: Show indifference to the lamb on Monday?

definitions.meaning: to snub or treat someone coldly
Sunday's roast joint, served cold the next day

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a joke: the shoulder of lamb roasted on Sunday is eaten cold on Monday.
explanation.definitionFit: To cold-shoulder someone is to ignore them deliberately; the leftover roast joke is literal cold meat.

clue.text: Expire, then arise miraculously when the Lord passes judgment?

parts.note: to expire is to die

indicators.note: a miracle transforms things, so these letters are transformed into a new order

explanation.surface: Death followed by a wondrous resurrection on Judgment Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miraculously' rearranges ARISE to give SIRAE. The Latin hymn's title means 'day of wrath', the Last Judgment.
explanation.definitionFit: Dies Irae is the medieval hymn describing the Day of Judgment, so it names that day.

clue.text: Marine sport makes Carol feel sick inside

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: to carol is to sing
to ail is to feel unwell

explanation.surface: Yachting leaves a woman named Carol queasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a woman's name, but it is the verb SING, holding AIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailing is a water sport practised at sea.

clue.text: Situation that's tricky, not right, with a part of the eye

indicators.note: not shows a letter being left out

parts.note: to be in a corner is to be in a tight spot

explanation.surface: A tricky situation involving damage to the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: CORNER loses one R to give CORNE, then A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: The cornea is the transparent front layer of the eye.

clue.text: Queen and king descending on a province

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece coming down on another sits above it

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province

explanation.surface: Royals swooping down on a region.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, R descends onto A and NI, so it comes first. Northern Ireland is often called 'the Province' in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A rani is an Indian queen or a rajah's wife.

clue.text: Film director embracing one back with old friends?

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: Carol Reed was the British director of The Third Man
a unit is one

explanation.surface: A director hugging someone returning to the company of old pals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like part of the wordplay, but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being reunited is coming back together with people you were once close to.

clue.text: Julian was such a mischief-maker hiding letters

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it within, so one piece sits inside the others

parts.note: Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin
letters arriving by mail are the post

explanation.surface: A Roman emperor described as a troublemaker who concealed his correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roman emperor Julian, who abandoned Christianity for the old gods, is known to history as Julian the Apostate. A and ATE hide POST.
explanation.definitionFit: Emperor Julian renounced his Christian faith, which earned him the historical epithet for a renegade from religion.

clue.text: A line at end of work is a little jewel

indicators.note: the following letters are placed after the piece for work, closing it off

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A single line at the end of a piece of writing shines like a small gem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At end of' puts A and L after OP.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is an iridescent gemstone, a classic small stone set in jewellery.

clue.text: Activity of water company that could be nationalised

indicators.note: these letters could be rearranged into something else, signalling a reworking of them

explanation.surface: A remark about utilities: what a water firm does might one day be taken into state ownership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' shows the letters of NATIONALISED being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing salt from seawater to make it drinkable is work a water supplier may undertake.

clue.text: Successful play that could be cheesy?

definitions.text: Successful play that could be cheesy?

parts.words: Successful play that could be cheesy?
parts.note: Agatha Christie's record-running London play, whose title names a device baited with cheese

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheesy' suggests a bad play, but the joke is that this play's name is a device baited with cheese. It has run in London since 1952.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-running Christie whodunit is named after a trap for rodents, which traditionally uses cheese as bait.

clue.text: Good person to have at wedding, one exuding enthusiasm

parts.note: an usher shows guests to their seats at a wedding

explanation.surface: A recommendation of a cheerful guest to invite to a marriage ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A gusher is a person who speaks with effusive, overflowing enthusiasm, like an oil well spouting.

clue.text: Retreat outside region where communities are often in conflict

definitions.text: where communities are often in conflict

indicators.note: one piece is placed outside another, wrapping round it

parts.note: a nest is a snug retreat or hideaway
an area is a region

explanation.surface: Withdrawal from a troubled zone where rival groups frequently clash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' splits the retreat word around the region; 'where communities are often in conflict' is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Near East, the lands of the eastern Mediterranean, is a region long known for strife between peoples.

clue.text: Lord taken in by exploit, hoodwinked

indicators.note: one piece is taken inside another, so it sits within it

parts.note: an exploit is a deed, a notable act
Lud is an old form of lord, as in 'm'lud' used to a judge

explanation.surface: A nobleman fooled by a daring stunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' doubles as fooled in the surface, but here 'taken in by' is the container signal. 'M'lud' is how British barristers address a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: To be deluded is to be deceived, tricked into believing something false.

clue.text: Went through cases for refuse dump initially

parts.note: to refuse is to decline

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone sorted boxes to throw into the tip at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like rubbish going to a dump, but it is the verb DECLINE, plus D.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, to decline a noun is to run through its cases.

clue.text: Of an artery could be aortic — different word ultimately!

indicators.note: the letters are made different, rearranged into a new order
ultimately points to the final letter of the word next to it

explanation.surface: A medical note: one artery name might be the main one's name with letters shuffled and a final change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Different' rearranges AORTIC; 'ultimately' adds the last letter of 'word', D.
explanation.definitionFit: Carotid describes the major arteries in the neck, so it means relating to a particular artery.

clue.text: Hearing Auntie doesn't like seeing one shrink?

definitions.meaning: a formal interview, as in an ... with the Pope

definitions.text: Auntie doesn't like seeing one shrink?
definitions.meaning: Auntie is a nickname for the BBC, which dislikes falling viewer figures

explanation.walkthrough: 'Auntie' is the British nickname for the BBC, which dreads a falling number of viewers or listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience is a formal hearing granted by a dignitary, and also the viewers a broadcaster wants to keep.

clue.text: Is a beautiful girl not English? A foreign girl

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: not shows a letter being left out

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: Asking whether a lovely girl is not English but foreign.
explanation.walkthrough: BELLE drops its E to give BELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabella is a girl's name of Spanish and Italian origin, so a foreign girl's name.

clue.text: Con good person going after an advantage

indicators.note: the piece for a good person goes after the others

parts.note: an gives A
a gain is an advantage
ST is short for saint, a good person

explanation.surface: A trickster with a good reputation chasing a profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Con' looks like a swindle, but it is the opposite of 'pro'.
explanation.definitionFit: In 'pros and cons', a con is an argument opposed to something.

clue.text: Stick around tot to offer protection

indicators.note: one piece goes around another, enclosing it

parts.note: to stick is to cling
to tot up is to add

explanation.surface: Holding on close to a small child to keep it safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a small child, but as a verb (tot up) it means sum; 'around' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cladding is a protective outer covering applied to a building or pipe.

clue.text: Natural venue in which one may have drunk and dined

parts.words: venue in which one may have drunk
parts.note: an inn is a place to drink
to have dined is to have eaten, ate

explanation.surface: A pub where one can drink and eat comes naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: Innate qualities are inborn, natural rather than learned.

clue.text: Anxiety in period without any sort of belief

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a day is a period of time
an ism is any doctrine or belief system

explanation.surface: Worry felt in a time when one has no faith at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as lacking, but in its older sense of outside it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismay is a feeling of alarm and distress, much like anxiety.

clue.text: Endlessly on the move, then bloke becomes immovable

indicators.note: something endless has its end removed, so the final letter goes

parts.note: in transit means travelling, on the move
a gent is a man, a bloke

explanation.surface: Someone constantly travelling turns into a person who will not budge.
explanation.walkthrough: IN TRANSIT loses its last letter to give INTRANSI. The surface's contrast between moving and immovable is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Intransigent means refusing to change one's views, unwilling to be moved.

clue.text: Restricted current through the loudspeaker

indicators.note: words heard through a speaker are spoken, so a word that sounds the same is wanted

parts.note: a tide is a current of water

explanation.surface: Electricity limited when passing through a speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' suggests electricity, but it is a water current.
explanation.definitionFit: Tied means bound or restricted, as in tied to a contract.

clue.text: Flowing water comes from river, not well

parts.note: someone not well is ill

explanation.surface: Running water drawn from a river rather than a well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not well' seems to contrast river with well-water, but it means ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A rill is a small stream, a narrow trickle of running water.

clue.text: Before, small children would be people cut off from society

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before
mites are small children

explanation.surface: In the past, little ones would have been isolated from everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Eremites are hermits, religious recluses who live apart from the world.

clue.text: The turn involving a stage performer

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to involve is to include, so one piece is wrapped round another

parts.note: a spin is a turn

explanation.surface: A music-hall act featuring an actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' suggests a variety act, fitting the stage; here it is SPIN, holding A.
explanation.definitionFit: A thespian is an actor, named after Thespis, the legendary first actor of ancient Greece.
